mechanism: Itraconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and may increase amoxicillin clavulanate exposure through clavulanic acid metabolism; additionally, both agents can cause gastrointestinal effects and amoxicillin may alter itraconazole absorption via pH changes.
action: Monitor for increased clavulanic acid-related side effects (GI upset, diarrhea) and ensure itraconazole is taken with adequate stomach acid; separate administration timing if GI intolerance develops.
